title: How the IB fits together
lead: PYP to MYP to DP: what happens in each year, the six subject groups, the core, and how points are awarded.

y9.title: Year 9 - MYP year 4
y9.body: No HL/SL yet. This is the foundation year: build study habits and keep language and mathematics strong.

y10.title: Year 10 - MYP year 5
y10.body: The Personal Project year, and the year the DP subject choice is actually made. This is when this tool is most useful.

y11.title: Year 11 - DP1
y11.body: All six subjects start, along with TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS.

y12.title: Year 12 - DP2
y12.body: Finish the Extended Essay and CAS; sit the May examinations.

tok.title: TOK (Theory of Knowledge)
tok.body: A course about how we know what we know. Graded A-E and, together with the Extended Essay, worth up to 3 additional points.

ee.title: EE (Extended Essay)
ee.body: An independent research essay. Graded A-E and, together with TOK, worth up to 3 additional points.

cas.title: CAS (Creativity, Activity, Service)
cas.body: Not graded, but it must be completed - an incomplete CAS means no diploma.

scoring.title: Scoring
scoring.body: 6 subjects x 7 points = 42, plus up to 3 points from TOK and the Extended Essay: {{max}} maximum, {{pass}} to pass.
scoring.source: Thresholds come from diploma-rules.json (last verified {{date}}) and are still marked as to be verified against the official IB documents.

considerations.title: Things to consider before choosing
considerations.lead: Workload, language choices, mathematics AA vs AI, and keeping doors open.

math-aa-vs-ai.title: Mathematics: AA or AI?
math-aa-vs-ai.body: AA leans towards pure mathematics and proof; AI leans towards modelling and applications. Most engineering, computer science, physical science and economics programmes expect AA - check each target programme's own page before deciding.

language-choice.title: Which language goes in Group 1?
language-choice.body: Group 1 is the student's best language, Group 2 is an additional language. If English is not the student's strongest language, putting the home language in Group 1 is often the steadier route. Note that New Zealand UE literacy needs English Language A (HL/SL) or English Language B (HL).

hl-workload.title: How heavy are three HLs?
hl-workload.body: Three HL subjects is the minimum and four is the maximum. Three heavy HLs (for example Mathematics AA, Physics and Chemistry) is a real workload - weigh it against the student's other commitments.

keep-doors-open.title: Keeping doors open
keep-doors-open.body: If the direction is still undecided, a balanced combination that includes HL Mathematics keeps the most pathways available. Dropping a science or mathematics to HL-free can close medicine and engineering later.

group6-swap.title: Replacing Group 6
group6-swap.body: The arts subject can be replaced by a second subject from Groups 1-4. Interdisciplinary subjects also exist: ESS satisfies Groups 3 and 4 at once, and Literature and Performance satisfies Groups 1 and 6.

school-offer.title: What the school actually offers
school-offer.body: A subject existing in the IB curriculum does not mean your school teaches it, and timetable blocks can rule out otherwise legal combinations. Confirm with the school's IB coordinator.

ee-cas-timing.title: When EE and CAS happen
ee-cas-timing.body: The Extended Essay topic is usually chosen in DP1 and finished in DP2; CAS runs across both years and must be completed for the diploma to be awarded.

changing-later.title: Changing subjects later
changing-later.body: Changes are possible early in DP1 but get progressively harder, which is why the Year 10 decision matters so much. Talk to the IB coordinator as early as possible.
